method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Hyperkalaemia = K over 5.5 mmol/L** (normal 3.5–5.0), **or over 6.0 mmol/L in neonates.**
claims.source_text: Serum potassium >5.5 mmol/L (normal range = 3.5-5.0 mmol/L), or Serum potassium >6.0 mmol/L in neonates
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severity (mmol/L):** mild 5.5–6.0 · moderate 6.1–7.0 · **severe over 7.0.**
claims.source_text: Severity Serum potassium (mmol/L) Mild 5.5-6.0 Moderate 6.1-7.0 Severe >7.0
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Moderate or severe hyperkalaemia can cause life-threatening arrhythmias and arrest: do an ECG and start cardiac monitoring. Stop any potassium-raising medications or fluids.**
claims.source_text: Moderate or severe hyperkalaemia can cause life-threatening arrhythmias and cardiac arrest. Perform an ECG and commence cardiac monitoring Stop any medications or fluids which cause hyperkalaemia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirm with a second sample** (collection artefact, e.g. a haemolysed sample, is a listed cause) — ⚠️ **but if the level is critically high and the scenario fits, treat before the repeat result.**
claims.source_text: Confirm potassium level with a second sample … If initial potassium level is critically high and hyperkalaemia is likely based on clinical scenario, initiate treatment before waiting for a repeat venous sample result … Artefact of collection process or technique (eg haemolysed sample)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ECG changes:** peaked T waves (early), prolonged PR, flattened or lost P waves, widened QRS, bradyarrhythmia and blocks; **severe: sine wave, ventricular arrhythmia, PEA, asystole.** ⚠️ **A normal ECG does not exclude arrhythmia risk.**
claims.source_text: Tall/peaked T wave (early) Prolonged PR interval Flattening, widening or loss of P wave Widening of QRS (increased risk of arrhythmia) Bradyarrhythmia, conduction blocks Severe hyperkalaemia: sine wave (fusion of QRS and T wave), ventricular arrhythmia, pulseless electrical activity, asystole … A normal ECG does not exclude risk for arrhythmia. Life threatening arrhythmia can occur without warning
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other tests:** UEC, glucose, venous gas, ± urine electrolytes; CK, cortisol/aldosterone (especially with hyponatraemia) or digoxin level as the cause suggests.
claims.source_text: Urea, creatinine and electrolytes Blood glucose level Venous blood gas +/- urine analysis and urinary electrolytes … CK Cortisol, aldosterone and hormonal precursor levels (particularly if hyponatraemia) Digoxin level (if relevant)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Calcium gluconate 10%: 0.15 mmol/kg (0.68 mL/kg), max 6.6 mmol (30 mL), slow IV/IO over 2–5 minutes if unstable, 15–20 minutes if stable.** Preferred with only a peripheral line.
claims.source_text: Calcium gluconate 10%: 0.15 mmol/kg, maximum 6.6 mmol (0.68 mL/kg, max 30 mL), slow IV/intraosseous injection over 2-5 minutes if unstable, 15-20 minutes if stable Preferable if only peripheral line available, as less irritant to veins
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Calcium chloride 10%: 0.14 mmol/kg (0.2 mL/kg), max 6.8 mmol (10 mL), slow IV/IO over 2–5 minutes if unstable, 15–20 minutes if stable.**
claims.source_text: Calcium chloride 10%: 0.14 mmol/kg, maximum 6.8 mmol (0.2 mL/kg, max 10 mL) slow IV/intraosseous injection over 2-5 minutes if unstable, over 15-20 minutes if stable
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stop if the heart rate drops significantly; watch for extravasation. Never give with bicarbonate; do not give in digoxin toxicity.**
claims.source_text: Continuous cardiac monitoring. Discontinue if heart rate drops significantly Monitor closely for extravasation Not to be given simultaneously with bicarbonate Not to be given if digoxin toxicity
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Onset under 3 minutes, lasts about 30 minutes.** The ECG should normalise; if not, repeat the dose (twice) or give an infusion titrated to response.
claims.source_text: Onset of action: <3 minutes. Should see normalisation of ECG. If not, repeat dose (twice) or IV infusion titrated to response Duration of action: approximately 30 minutes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Nebulised salbutamol:** 25 kg or less 2.5 mg; over 25 kg 5 mg (max 10–20 mg); **1–2-hourly.** Onset 30 minutes, lasts 2–3 hours.
claims.source_text: Salbutamol via nebuliser ≤25 kg: 2.5 mg neb 1-2 hourly >25 kg: 5 mg neb (max 10-20 mg) 1-2 hourly Onset of action: 30 minutes Duration of action: 2-3 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **IV salbutamol only if severe and after discussion with a senior clinician**; monitor for tachycardia.
claims.source_text: Only consider salbutamol IV if severe hyperkalaemia AND after discussion with senior clinician. Monitor for tachycardia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe: glucose 10% 5 mL/kg IV bolus (if no hyponatraemia) plus short-acting insulin 0.1 unit/kg IV bolus (max 10 units)**, followed by an insulin/glucose infusion.
claims.source_text: Severe hyperkalaemia Glucose 10% 5 mL/kg IV bolus (if no hyponatraemia) Insulin short acting (eg Actrapid®) 0.1 unit/kg IV bolus (max 10 units) Followed by insulin/glucose infusion (see below)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Moderate: glucose 10% with 0.9% sodium chloride at maintenance rate plus short-acting insulin infusion 0.1 unit/kg/hour IV.**
claims.source_text: Moderate hyperkalaemia Glucose 10% with 0.9% sodium chloride IV at maintenance rate Insulin short acting (eg Actrapid®) infusion: 0.1 unit/kg/hour IV
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **High risk of insulin error: dilute 10 units (0.1 mL) to 10 mL with 0.9% sodium chloride (1 unit/mL) and draw the dose from that. Check glucose every 30–60 minutes.**
claims.source_text: Insulin vials are highly concentrated in relation to dosage and have a high risk of medication error … To safely prepare the insulin dose, first dilute 10 units of insulin (= 0.1 mL) to a total of 10 mL with sodium chloride 0.9% to make a final concentration of 1 unit/mL. Withdraw the prescribed insulin dose from this 1 unit/mL solution Close monitoring of glucose every 30-60 minutes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sodium bicarbonate — metabolic acidosis only.** Severe hyperkalaemia with acidosis: 8.4% 1–3 mmol/kg (1–3 mL/kg) IV over 5 minutes. Mild–moderate with acidosis: 1 mmol/kg (1 mL/kg) slow IV over 30 minutes. ⚠️ **Not with calcium.**
claims.source_text: Bicarbonate In metabolic acidosis only Severe hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 1 mmol/mL: administer 1-3 mmol/kg (1-3 mL/kg) IV over 5 minutes Mild to moderate hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis Sodium bicarbonate 8.4% 1 mmol/mL: administer 1 mmol/kg (1 mL/kg) slow IV infusion over 30 minutes Do NOT give simultaneously with calcium
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Polystyrene sulfonate resin 0.5–1 g/kg (max 30 g) 6-hourly PR or oral (with lactulose)** — mild effect, multiple doses needed. Separate from other oral medicines by at least 3 hours.
claims.source_text: Mild effect, multiple doses necessary, may be used as long-term agent Sodium polystyrene sulfonate (Resonium A®) or calcium polystyrene sulfonate (Calcium Resonium®) 0.5-1 g/kg 6 hourly (max 30 g) PR or oral (with lactulose) … Separate oral administration from other oral medications by at least 3 hours
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use resins with ileus, recent abdominal surgery, perforation or hypernatraemia.**
claims.source_text: Not to be used if ileus, recent abdominal surgery, perforation, or hypernatraemia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dialysis:** organise with the paediatric renal or intensive care team and transfer to a tertiary centre.
claims.source_text: Dialysis To be organised with local paediatric renal or intensive care team. Transfer to tertiary centre
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team for all moderate or severe hyperkalaemia**, or an underlying cause such as renal abnormality. **Seek specialist advice if there is renal disease or complex co-morbidity.**
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when All children with moderate or severe hyperkalaemia Underlying medical cause eg renal abnormalities … Seek specialist advice for children with underlying renal disease or complex co-morbidities
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer for all severe hyperkalaemia and anyone needing dialysis.**
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when All children with severe hyperkalaemia All children requiring dialysis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** when potassium is normal and stable, the child is asymptomatic with a normal ECG, and the cause is treated.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Potassium level is normal and stable Child is asymptomatic with normal ECG Cause of hyperkalaemia identified and treated adequately
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hyperkalaemia' (Last updated August 2024), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hyperkalaemia/, retrieved 2026-09-23
